data.title: Everplay Group: Strong Momentum, Discount Valuation Support Buy Rating with Unchanged $380 Price Target
data.description:
James Wheatcroft, an analyst from Jefferies, maintained the Buy rating on everplay Group. The associated price target remains the same with p380.00.

James Wheatcroft has given his Buy rating due to a combination of factors that highlight everplay Group’s strong operational momentum and attractive valuation. Recent flagship launches such as Hell Let Loose: Vietnam and Wardogs have significantly outperformed prior records, with Wardogs surpassing one million units sold and reaching very high concurrent user levels, prompting management to guide FY26 results meaningfully above current market expectations.

In addition, the company’s large and resilient back catalogue, fast-growing StoryToys segment, increased strategic stake in Super Media Group, and solid net cash position support both organic growth and potential value-accretive M&A and dividends. Against this backdrop, everplay still trades at a discount EV/EBITDA multiple versus peers, leading Wheatcroft to reaffirm his Buy recommendation with an unchanged price target of $380, reflecting confidence in both earnings upgrades and re-rating potential.

data.description:

Michael Nedelcovych has given his Buy rating due to a combination of factors tied to Johnson & Johnson’s oncology strength and portfolio optimization. The strong final overall-survival data from the PAPILLON trial reinforce Rybrevant as a leading option in EGFR Ex20ins NSCLC, with meaningful durability of benefit that should support its use beyond this niche setting.

This clinical momentum, together with the improved safety and convenience profile of Rybrevant Faspro and its emerging potential in broader oncology indications, underpins a favorable growth outlook. data.title: Macy’s: Early Margin and Merchandising Gains Tempered by Traffic and Category Risks Keep Oliver Chen at Hold
data.description:
In a report released yesterday, Oliver Chen from TD Cowen maintained a Hold rating on Macy’s, with a price target of $25.00.

Oliver Chen has given his Hold rating due to a combination of factors tied to Macy’s recent progress and remaining uncertainties. He sees clear evidence that product upgrades and better brand assortments are driving higher average selling prices and solid comparable sales across Macy’s, Bloomingdale’s, and Bluemercury, with gross margin and SG&A showing modest but positive leverage.

At the same time, Chen is cautious about the durability of this momentum, particularly as Macy’s faces tougher upcoming comparisons and ongoing pressure in traffic conversion and certain weaker categories. He also wants further confirmation that multiple margin levers—such as inventory productivity, private label growth, and supply chain efficiencies—can consistently translate into stronger profitability, leading him to a balanced Hold stance rather than a more aggressive rating.
